findings.title: Object URL for backup codes download is never revoked on close
findings.body: backupCodesUrl is created with URL.createObjectURL and only revoked when handleSetup is invoked again. There is no cleanup on modal close (onOpenChange / Cancel button), no useEffect cleanup, and resetState() does not reset backupCodesUrl. Each successful setup leaks a Blob and its object URL (containing the plaintext backup codes) for the lifetime of the page. Add a useEffect cleanup that calls URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl) on unmount/close, and revoke inside resetState.

findings.title: Stale internal state shown after closing the modal with the X button
findings.body: Dialog's onOpenChange (the X / overlay close path) does not call resetState(). The component remains mounted with the previous step, dataUri, secret and backupCodes. Reopening the modal after closing it via X can show an old QR code, old TOTP secret and the previously generated backup codes. resetState should be invoked from onOpenChange (or equivalent), and the displayed data should be cleared when the modal is dismissed without completion.

findings.title: twoFactorLostAccess not reset when disable modal is closed via X
findings.body: The twoFactorLostAccess state is only reset after a successful disable. Closing the dialog with the X button (onOpenChange) does not reset it, so the next time the modal is opened the BackupCode input is shown instead of the TOTP input. Reset twoFactorLostAccess (and clear the form/values) when the dialog is closed without a successful submit.

findings.title: JSON.parse of decrypted backup codes has no error handling
findings.body: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)) will throw if the stored ciphertext is corrupted, the encryption key is rotated, or the data shape is unexpected. An uncaught throw here aborts the entire authorize() callback and surfaces as an InternalServerError, locking the user out. Wrap the decrypt + JSON.parse in try/catch and convert failures into a clean ErrorCode (e.g. MissingBackupCodes or InternalServerError) so authentication degrades gracefully.

findings.title: JSON.parse of decrypted backup codes has no error handling
findings.body: Same issue as in next-auth-options.ts: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is unguarded. A corrupt/rotated backupCodes blob will crash the disable endpoint with an uncaught exception (500), preventing the user from disabling 2FA. Catch the error and return a typed error (e.g. MissingBackupCodes) instead.

findings.title: Backup code is not atomically consumed; concurrent logins can reuse a code
findings.body: The backup code is looked up with backupCodes.indexOf(...) and then nulled out in a separate prisma.user.update. Between the read and the write, two concurrent signIn attempts (e.g. two browser tabs) can both observe the same code at the same index, both null it, and both be authenticated, allowing a single-use backup code to be used more than once. The same race exists in disable.ts (the indexOf succeeds but the consumed code is only later wiped by the unconditional backupCodes: null in the final update). Use a conditional update (e.g. updateMany where the code is still present, or store used codes with a unique marker) so consumption is atomic.

findings.title: BackupCode component is exported as default function TwoFactor
findings.body: The file apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx declares `export default function TwoFactor(...)`. Two other components in this PR are also named TwoFactor (apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx and EnableTwoFactorModal imports it). The mismatch causes confusion in stack traces / DevTools and creates a real collision risk if anyone re-exports these modules together. Rename the function to BackupCode (or BackupCodeInput) to match the file name and the other new component.

findings.title: formatBackupCode referenced before it is defined
findings.body: handleSetup uses formatBackupCode at line 95, but formatBackupCode is declared as a const at line 163, below the handler. This works only because handleSetup is invoked asynchronously after render. It is fragile (moving handleSetup to a hook or memoizing it would TDZ-crash) and makes the file hard to read. Move the formatBackupCode declaration above its first use.

findings.title: backupCodes state is implicitly typed as never[]
findings.body: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` infers never[], so .map(formatBackupCode) on body.backupCodes only compiles because body.backupCodes is any. There is no compile-time guarantee that the state actually contains strings, and the explicit type <string[]>([]) (or the inferred type from body.backupCodes) would catch a future API shape change.

findings.title: Exhausted backup codes surface as IncorrectBackupCode, not MissingBackupCodes
findings.body: After a user has consumed all backup codes, the stored JSON array consists entirely of nulls. backupCodes.indexOf(...) still returns -1, so the user is told IncorrectBackupCode rather than MissingBackupCodes (and they cannot tell that they have no codes left). Detect the all-null case (e.g. !backupCodes.some(Boolean)) and throw ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes before the indexOf check.

findings.title: No end-to-end coverage for backup code login or backup code disable
findings.body: The PR introduces an entire authentication path (login with backup code, disable 2FA with backup code, marking codes as used) that has no e2e coverage. The TODO at line 12 acknowledges this, but the new code paths are exactly where regressions are most dangerous (auth bypass, accidental single-use violation). Add at minimum: (1) login with a backup code (and confirm the code is consumed), (2) login with a previously-used backup code fails with IncorrectBackupCode, (3) disabling 2FA via the 'Lost access' button with a backup code.

findings.title: Continue button at QR step has misleading type=submit and onClick
findings.body: The QR step Continue button is declared `type="submit"` and `onClick={() => setStep(SetupStep.EnterTotpCode)}`. It lives inside <Form handleSubmit={handleEnable} ...>, so clicking it both fires handleEnable (which sends a request to /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable with whatever stale totpCode is still in the form, or undefined) and changes the step. The visible behavior appears to work only because the enable endpoint errors out when 2FA is already enabled, but this is an unintended API call. Use type="button" here so clicking it does not submit the form.
